newsitem.title: UK: Dlr at current level at end-97 - BOT Mitsubishi poll.
newsitem.headline: Dlr at current level at end-97 - BOT Mitsubishi poll.

text.p: Currency dealers in London expect the dollar to be fairly close to its current levels against the mark and yen at the end of 1997, according to a poll by Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi.

The survey, which polled people attending the Japanese bank's annual forex party here on Wednesday, showed an average forecast of 121.31 yen and 1.7165 marks for the dollar's rate at the end of this year.
Predictions by the 169 attendees, including eight central bankers, for the dollar's rate at the year-end fell in a range of 97.00-148.00 yen and 1.4200-2.0457 marks.
Asked how far they thought the dollar would rise this year they said, on average, that it would peak at 131.98 yen and 1.8044 marks.
So far this year, the currency has hit a four-year peak of 124.82 yen and a 34-month high of 1.7050 marks, both of which were reached in the past week.
Ranges for forecasts for the dollar's highest rate in 1997 were 125.30-165.00 yen and 1.7050-2.1000 marks.
The dollar stood at 122.85/90 yen and 1.6850/55 marks at 1404 GMT.
Concerning how far the mark could rise against the yen in 1997, their predictions averaged 77.21 yen and fell into a range of 67.47-96.00. Mark/yen was quoted at 72.92/95 at 1404 GMT.
